question: What limitation remains in the conceptual level of the śākta means?
premises: In the śākta means there is a conceptual level grounded in awareness of agency.
When awareness of agency becomes clear, that level is operative.
Even in that śākta level, contraction remains because of the previous method.
inference: The śākta means includes a conceptual awareness of agency, but it still carries contraction inherited from the lower āṇava method.
uncertainties: pūrvanītitaḥ may refer specifically to āṇavopāya or more generally to any prior procedure.
plain_english: Thus, in the śākta means there is a conceptual level consisting in the awareness of being an agent. When that awareness is clear, this level is present; yet even here there is still contraction, carried over from the previous method.
